summary: Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He earned a bachelor's from Columbia University and a Ph.D. from Graduate Theological Union. He held teaching posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Loyola University Chicago, and several other institutions.

Taijun Inokuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts as lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987) at Ryukoku University, and representative of The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. He taught at Komazawa University and served as professor of Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo.
Taiken Kyuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Vienna by 1999 and served as an associate professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hiroshima University. He served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Taikyo Tanigawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Koyasan University and earned a Ph.D. from Toyo University in 1994, holding assistant professor and professor posts at Koyasan University (attested 1980–2026).
Taion Satomi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University until 1933 and served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).

Taira Shidehara (1870–1953) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1891 to 1894, later holding posts at the University of Tokyo (circa 1900–1902) and Tokyo University of Education (circa 1902–1906).

Tairyo Makita (1912–2011) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto Universities. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1949–1976), professor at Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University, and president of Saitama Institute of Technology.
Tairyu Tsunoda works in Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

Taisei Iwata is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), a professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and an advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Taisen Deshimaru (1914–1982) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kodo Sawaki from circa 1936 to 1965 and founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and earned a master's degree from the University of Tokyo, later serving as professor at Komazawa University (circa 1976–2006) and lecturer at the Eastern Institute.
Taishun Mibu (1913–1980) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Taisho University until 1937 and later served there as library director (attested 1972).

Taitetsu Unno (1929–2014) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo (M.A., Ph.D.), and served as Jill Ker Conway Professor of Religion at Smith College (1971–1998).
Taitsu Kono is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Mumon Yamada. He later held an academic post at Hanazono University from circa 1993 to 2001.

Taixu (1890–1947) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy figure who studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Renshan Yang at Jinling Scriptural Press. He led the Minnan Buddhist Institute (1927) and founded several Buddhist institutes and organizations.

Taizan Maezumi (1931–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, and San Francisco State University under Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission from 1956.
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. Sze earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).
